name: Bela
overview: Bela was a male Edomite who served as king over the Edomites. He is uniquely identified as the king whose city was Dinhabah, establishing his significance in the governance of Edom as recorded in Genesis 36:32. No additional personal notes are provided.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Bela' means 'swallower' or 'devourer,' reflecting a proper name of Hebrew origin as noted in Genesis 36:32. This meaning may imply a strong or formidable character, though the text does not elaborate further.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Bela was the son of Beor, establishing a direct familial link important for understanding his lineage within Edomite royalty as stated in Genesis 36:32. Beyond this, no other family relationships are noted.
scriptureSignificance: Bela's significance lies in his role as an early king of Edom, marking the establishment of monarchy among the Edomites. His reign from the city of Dinhabah represents a foundational moment in Edomite history, illustrating the development of political structures outside of Israel. This highlights the broader biblical narrative of neighboring nations and their leadership.
